overview: Systematic review with meta-analysis of comparative studies of haemolysis in blood drawn through peripheral intravenous catheters versus venepuncture, registered before screening, with pre-specified subgroups by technique, catheter gauge, collector training and transport.
population: Blood samples from adults and children in emergency or acute care settings in comparative studies of any design (randomised, crossover, cohort, before-after and cross-sectional).
exposure: Collection through a newly inserted or existing peripheral intravenous catheter, with tube type or syringe recorded.
procedures: Librarian-designed searches of three databases and conference proceedings from 2000 to 2026 under agreement LIB-LAB-2025. Two reviewers (the quality lead and the trainee) screen and extract independently, resolving disagreements by discussion. Risk of bias is assessed with RoB 2 for randomised comparisons and ROBINS-I for non-randomised ones; certainty is rated with GRADE for each outcome.

outcomes.name: Haemolysis
outcomes.measure: Proportion of samples with haemolysis, preferring analyser index definitions; odds ratio for catheter versus venepuncture
outcomes.why: The outcome that causes rejection and repeat draws.

outcomes.name: Sample rejection or redraw
outcomes.measure: Proportion of samples rejected or redrawn

outcomes.name: Potassium difference
outcomes.measure: Mean difference in potassium between paired samples
outcomes.why: Shows whether haemolysis changes clinical decisions.

outcomes.name: Additional needle sticks
outcomes.measure: Extra punctures per patient under venepuncture-only strategies, where reported
outcomes.why: The cost to patients of avoiding catheter draws.

feasibility: About 80 hours between two reviewers: 10 for search refinement with the librarian, 30 for dual screening, 25 for extraction and risk of bias, 15 for analysis and writing.
biasMitigation: Separate analysis of randomised and non-randomised studies
Sensitivity analysis restricted to analyser index definitions
Funnel plot and small-study test if ten or more studies

biasFlags.label: Confounding by indication in non-randomised studies
biasFlags.note: Patients with difficult access get catheter draws; analysed separately from randomised studies.

biasFlags.label: Heterogeneous haemolysis definitions
biasFlags.note: Sensitivity analysis on analyser index definitions.

biasFlags.label: Publication bias
biasFlags.note: Conference abstracts searched; small-study test if enough studies.

flags: Four pre-specified effect modifiers and no others
parsimony.simplestPath: One comparison, one primary outcome, four pre-specified subgroups.

theoreticalFramework: GRADE for certainty; no other framework.
summary: Registered systematic review with one primary outcome and four pre-specified effect modifiers.
